hook: You picked up your phone to check the time and put it down 25 minutes later.
body:
**You picked up your phone to check the time. You put it down 25 minutes later. You have no memory of what you just looked at.**

That is not a attention problem. That is a trigger-behaviour loop running without your input.

Your brain registered a micro-moment of discomfort — maybe boredom, maybe a pause in a task — and executed a learned reflex. The phone was the nearest exit. You did not decide to pick it up. The environment decided for you.

This happens over 100 times a day for the average person. Most of those pickups are not decisions. They are reflexes that have been practised into automation.

The fix is not willpower. Willpower engages after the reflex has already fired. You need to change what the environment makes easy before the moment of decision arrives.

Put friction between you and the phone. Charger in another room. Lock screen with no apps. Distance, not discipline.

The reflex cannot fire if the exit is not there.

I put the full architecture system in the link in bio — it is free.
